title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

reports.title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

summary:
Matthew and Leah Spurlock were stopped twice because their Kansas KU Alumni license plate, number 7007, matched a stolen temporary tag on a GMC pickup. First, Colwich police pulled Leah over after a Flock camera flagged her minivan as possibly stolen, but officers realized the wrong plate type had been entered. About a month later, police in Catoosa, Oklahoma, stopped the couple at gunpoint and handcuffed Matthew after another Flock camera alert. The cameras read only the numbers and letters, not the plate background, and Kansas duplicates numbers across more than 100 plate designs.

Wichita police Captain Casey Slaughter said Flock alerts alone are not enough for a stop, but if a stolen tag is confirmed, officers have no choice. Kansas is moving from six digit to seven digit license plate numbers to prevent duplicates, which Slaughter said would give peace of mind. The Spurlocks are no longer worried because the stolen vehicle entry expired, and they plan to keep their plate.
